# Animal Tissue Master Practice Exam (50 Questions — Mixed MCQs & MSQs)

### PE_T1_01 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), identify the French anatomist who defined 21 primary tissue types without microscopic aid:

- A) Xavier Bichat
- B) Marcello Malpighi
- C) Robert Hooke
- D) Anton van Leeuwenhoek

> **✅ Answer:** A) Xavier Bichat
> **Explanation:** Xavier Bichat coined the term tissue and defined 21 primary tissue classes.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="[Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Pract" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T1_02 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), microscopic investigation of animal tissues was systematically pioneered by which biologist?

- A) Xavier Bichat
- B) Marcello Malpighi
- C) Theodor Schwann
- D) Rudolf Virchow

> **✅ Answer:** B) Marcello Malpighi
> **Explanation:** Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic histology.

### PE_T1_03 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), true tissue level of organization first evolved in which invertebrate phylum?

- A) Porifera
- B) Coelenterata (Cnidaria)
- C) Platyhelminthes
- D) Annelida

> **✅ Answer:** B) Coelenterata (Cnidaria)
> **Explanation:** Tissue grade organization originated in Coelenterates (Hydra).

### PE_T1_04 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), embryonic mesoderm gives origin to which pair of primary tissues?

- A) Epithelial and Nervous
- B) Connective and Muscular
- C) Epithelial and Muscular
- D) Connective and Nervous

> **✅ Answer:** B) Connective and Muscular
> **Explanation:** Connective tissue and muscle arise from embryonic mesoderm.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="[Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Pract" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T1_05 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), which primary tissue type originates from all three germ layers (Ectoderm, Mesoderm, Endoderm)?

- A) Muscular Tissue
- B) Nervous Tissue
- C) Epithelial Tissue
- D) Connective Tissue

> **✅ Answer:** C) Epithelial Tissue
> **Explanation:** Epithelia derive from ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.

### PE_T1_06 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), the non-cellular basement membrane underlying epithelial sheets contains basal lamina and:

- A) Reticular lamina
- B) Hydroxyapatite matrix
- C) Elastic lamellae
- D) Ossein canals

> **✅ Answer:** A) Reticular lamina
> **Explanation:** Basement membrane = Basal lamina + Reticular lamina.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="[Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Pract" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T1_07 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), avascular epithelial sheets obtain metabolic nutrients primarily via:

- A) Direct intra-epithelial capillary blood flow
- B) Simple diffusion from underlying connective tissue blood vessels
- C) Active transport from lumen air space
- D) Perichondrial canaliculi

> **✅ Answer:** B) Simple diffusion from underlying connective tissue blood vessels
> **Explanation:** Epithelial cells depend on nutrient diffusion across the basement membrane.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="[Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Pract" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T1_08 (MSQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1 - MSQ), select all historical milestones established in animal histology: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Xavier Bichat defined 21 primary tissue types without microscope
- [ ] B) Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic tissue investigation
- [ ] C) Mayer coined the term 'Histology' in 1819
- [ ] D) True tissue level first evolved in Phylum Coelenterata
- [ ] E) Leeuwenhoek discovered Haversian osteons

> **✅ Answers (Multiple Select):** A) Xavier Bichat defined 21 primary tissue types without microscope, B) Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic tissue investigation, C) Mayer coined the term 'Histology' in 1819, D) True tissue level first evolved in Phylum Coelenterata
> **Explanation:** Bichat, Malpighi, Mayer, and Coelenterate evolution represent foundational histology milestones.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="[Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Pract" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

- [ ] A) Epithelial Tissue
- [ ] B) Connective Tissue
- [ ] C) Muscular Tissue
- [ ] D) Nervous Tissue

### PE_T4_10 (MSQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4 - MSQ), select all connective tissue sheaths organizing skeletal muscle blocks: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Endomysium (enclosing single muscle fiber)

- [ ] D) Perichondrium
- [ ] E) Periosteum

> **✅ Answers (Multiple Select):** A) Endomysium (enclosing single muscle fiber), B) Perimysium (enclosing muscle fascicle bundle), C) Epimysium (enclosing whole muscle belly)
> **Explanation:** Muscle sheaths = Endomysium, Perimysium, Epimysium.

### PE_T5_01 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), the metabolic cell body of a neurone containing the nucleus is the:

- A) Axon
- B) Cyton / Soma
- C) Dendrite
- D) Synaptic knob

> **✅ Answer:** B) Cyton / Soma
> **Explanation:** Cyton (Soma) is the main cell body of a neurone.

### PE_T5_02 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules in cyton and dendrites consist of clumps of:

- A) Smooth ER and lipids
- B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
- C) Lysosomes and Golgi bodies
- D) Microtubules and centrioles

> **✅ Answer:** B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
> **Explanation:** Nissl's granules are RER and free ribosomes synthesizing protein.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="[Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Pract" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T5_03 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules are strictly ABSENT in:

- A) Cyton
- B) Axon and Axon Hillock
- C) Main dendrites
- D) Soma cytoplasm

> **✅ Answer:** B) Axon and Axon Hillock
> **Explanation:** Nissl's granules are absent in axon hillock and axon.

### PE_T5_04 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), saltatory nerve impulse propagation leaps along myelinated axons at:

- A) Synaptic knobs
- B) Uninsulated Nodes of Ranvier
- C) Schwann cell nuclei
- D) Axon hillock

> **✅ Answer:** B) Uninsulated Nodes of Ranvier
> **Explanation:** Action potentials jump from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier.

### PE_T5_05 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), which CNS neuroglia construct the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)?

- A) Astrocytes
- B) Oligodendrocytes
- C) Microglia
- D) Ependymal cells

> **✅ Answer:** A) Astrocytes
> **Explanation:** Astrocytes form perivascular end-feet creating the Blood-Brain Barrier.

### PE_T5_06 (MCQ): [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), myelin sheath in the Central Nervous System (CNS) is synthesized by:

- A) Schwann cells
- B) Oligodendrocytes
- C) Astrocytes
- D) Microglia

> **✅ Answer:** B) Oligodendrocytes
> **Explanation:** Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin; Schwann cells form PNS myelin.

- A) Astrocytes
